title: Frozen sandbox manifest
description: What the sandbox episode found it takes to run this app, written once at the end of setup's phase 2 and changed only by an amendment episode. Gates and roles read it from the default branch. The episode is an agent's work; this file is what makes its result reviewable and reproducible.

tier.description: How far verification can go here. renders: the app starts and a browser sees it working. build_and_test: it builds and its tests run, but it cannot be started. static: neither, so only static checks apply. Gates may claim no more than the tier allows.

tier_reason.description: Why this tier and not the one above it. Required in practice below renders, because the user should know what stopped it.

commands.description: Each command the episode ran successfully, or null when this repo has none (no tests, say). Null is a fact about the repo; a missing manifest means the factory does not know.

coverage.description: The tests, run so they also write a coverage report at coverage_report.path. When set, the tests gate runs this instead of `test`, once.

app_url.description: Where the running app answers inside the sandbox, when the tier is renders.

env.description: Every variable the sandbox is given, and nothing else is: the environment is closed, so a variable missing here is absent in the sandbox rather than inherited from the runner, and the app fails loudly instead of reaching something real.

kind.description: self: the app's own configuration, set to its correct value (its origin, a domain allowlist). service: points at a throwaway service in the sandbox. stub: points at a local fake that behaves like a third party. test_mode: a provider's own test credential. inert: present so the app starts; any path needing it cannot work here.

value.description: The literal value, for anything that is not a secret.

secret.description: The name of the repository secret that supplies the value. Never the value.

items.description: A literal value or the name of a secret, never both: oneOf fails when both branches match.

env.description: The service's own configuration, e.g. a throwaway database password. Never a real credential.

ready.description: How to tell the service is up: a TCP port check by default.

egress.description: Hosts the sandbox may reach beyond the package registries. Safe to list because no credential of the user's is present.

stubs.description: Local fakes for third parties the sandbox cannot reach. A fixture captured from a real API goes stale, so where it came from and when is recorded, and staleness is visible rather than discovered.

hosts.description: Hosts this stub answers for at their own address, for clients the app cannot point elsewhere. The sandbox resolves them to this runner and presents a certificate for them from a CA made for the run.

port.description: The plain-HTTP port the stub listens on; requests for its hosts are forwarded here.

start.description: How to start the stub, from the repo root, with PORT set.

dropped.description: Instructions from the repo's own container or deploy config that were deliberately not carried into the sandbox, with why. They describe what production does, not what the app needs installed.

capabilities.description: What verification here can and cannot exercise. The verifier compares a change's paths against this, and a change touching something listed under not_exercised is the signal that opens an amendment episode.

episode.description: Each attempt the agent made: what it tried, what it saw, what it changed. Short, because it is read by people deciding whether to trust the result.

amended_by.description: The inadequacy reports that opened amendment episodes, newest last.

coverage_report.description: Where commands.coverage writes its report, and in which format. The trial checks the report parses.

static_checks.description: Checkers this repo's own toolchain runs, each writing SARIF. The static gate counts their findings per rule per file, alongside the checkers it knows. The trial checks each one runs and its SARIF parses.

dependencies.description: Everything outside its own code the app needs to work, each with the stand-in the sandbox uses and the request that proves the stand-in works. The trial runs every probe; a dependency whose probe fails, or that has none, is not exercised, and the freeze lists it under capabilities.not_exercised.

oneOf.description: How the trial proves this dependency works in the sandbox: a request to the running app that only succeeds when the stand-in works. It passes when the app answers 2xx at this same path, without redirecting elsewhere, and shows expect_text if given.

signed_in.description: Sent with the session sign_in mints.

proven.description: Set by the freeze from the trial: whether the probe passed.

sign_in.description: How the roles get a signed-in session without going through the identity provider, whose pages their browser cannot reach. The command runs from the repo root in the sandbox's environment once the app answers, and prints JSON: {"cookies": [{"name", "value", "path"?, "httpOnly"?, "secure"?, "sameSite"?}]} — a session for a throwaway test user, made the way the app's own auth makes one (a row in the sandbox database, a token signed with the sandbox's own secret). The runner sets each cookie's domain.

ui_paths.description: Globs for the files that make up the UI. A product-work PR that changes one of them must carry a video; setup finds them by looking for the directories that depend on a UI framework.
